summary: Tracing tools can construct an effort fingerprint from model calls, retries, evaluation passes, and infrastructure use. They measure process, not quality; the signal becomes useful only after calibration against independent outcomes for comparable tasks.

items.text: MLflow Tracing exposes token usage and estimated cost per LLM span and aggregated trace, allowing productive calls, evaluator calls, and repeated attempts to be analyzed separately.

LangSmith's trace tree breaks usage and cost into input, output, reasoning, tool, and retrieval runs and aggregates by project or thread; this supports a structured effort fingerprint rather than one spend number.

OpenTelemetry generative-AI attributes standardize operation, provider, model, and token-usage fields across instrumentation, making longitudinal calibration less dependent on one observability vendor.

OpenCost allocates Kubernetes resource use and cost by workload and labels, so self-hosted inference, evaluation workers, and accelerator time can join the fingerprint even when no provider token bill exists.
